articles.title: Odisha govt evacuates nearly 50,000 people as cyclone 'Akvan' shifts course towards state
articles.summary: Bhubaneswar: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi on Wednesday said around 50,000 people have so far been evacuated to safety ahead of the likely landfall of severe cyclonic storm 'Akvan' between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in the eastern state. Majhi, who presided over a high-level review meeting on the preparedness of the state government, said the highest number of people will be evacuated from Ganjam district and the process is underway. “Our target is zero casualties and the evacuation drive has been launched in a massive manner, both in the plains and hilly terrain,” he said. People were being shifted to safer locations from several villages of Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts, the CM said. The state government has set up 3,000 cyclone shelters, of which 448 were already operational, Majhi said. Cyclone Akvan intensifies into severe cyclonic storm, landfall between Machilipatnam and Puri on Nov 20 Odisha has allocated Rs 20 crore to 15 districts to carry out relief and rescue operations. Majhi said the IMD has issued a warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in 11 districts for Thursday and Friday – Malkangiri, Koraput, Rayagada, Kalahandi, Gajapati, Ganjam, Kandhamal, Boudh, Puri, Nayagarh and Khurda. The average wind speed along the Odisha coast would be around 100 kmph, he said. The Odisha government has also announced the closure of schools in six districts for three days from Thursday – Ganjam, Gajapati, Puri, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara and Kandhamal – suspended leaves of employees, and deployed senior bureaucrats in vulnerable areas in the wake of the approaching cyclone.

articles.title: Delhi-Tokyo talks to coincide with Trump-Xi meet; Japan explores using missile test range in India
articles.summary: New Delhi: With Japan exploring the possibility of using facilities in India for live-fire training involving its long-range missiles, New Delhi and Tokyo will seek to deepen defence cooperation in areas including joint development of warships, mine-countermeasure capabilities and transfer of stealth-enhancing naval technology on Thursday – the day United States President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping. The India-Japan 2+2 ministerial dialogue in Tokyo will also focus on securing critical infrastructure, addressing vulnerabilities in global supply chains and connectivity chokepoints, and building resilient supply chains in key sectors amid growing geopolitical uncertainties and speculation about a US pivot away from the Indo-Pacific region. “Whether it is resources or energy, market access or technology, or indeed even finance, every aspect of global economic activity has been more and more openly weaponised by relevant players. Chokepoints and gateways, whether physical or virtual, have similarly become subject to strategic agendas,” External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said in Tokyo on Wednesday. “The era of rules, norms and assumptions is unfortunately rapidly eroding.” He said that India and Japan were not only two major democracies in Asia but also dynamic market economies and maritime nations, and hence “indispensable in shaping a free, open and rules-based Indo-Pacific”. Jaishankar will join Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in the 2+2 dialogue with their Japanese counterparts, Toshimitsu Motegi and Shinjiro Koizumi, in Tokyo on Thursday. Japan is exploring the possibility of using a military firing range in India for live-fire training involving its long-range surface-to-ship missiles, including the Type-25 anti-ship missile, and small attack drones. Tokyo sent military officials to India last month to assess the feasibility. General Masayoshi Arai, the chief of Japan Ground Self-Defence Force, recently confirmed that the two sides were exploring the possibility. Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi seeks deeper ties with India The Type-25 missile, with a reported range of around 1,000 km, is part of Japan's efforts to develop the ability to strike targets from a safe distance. However, Japan's limited geographical area makes it difficult to find sufficiently large and safe training zones for firing long-range missiles without risking interference with civilian air and maritime traffic, prompting it to explore the use of overseas military ranges, including facilities in India. New Delhi had first agreed to facilitate a foreign country's access to its military testing infrastructure in 2019, when it had exchanged a Letter of Intent with Singapore committing to conclude a Memorandum of Understanding to enable the Southeast Asian nation's use of the Integrated Test Range at Chandipur off the eastern coast of India. Any similar arrangement between New Delhi and Tokyo, which share a strategic partnership, could cause unease in Beijing, particularly as China has territorial disputes with both – with India over the entire stretch of the boundary and with Japan over the Senkaku Islands, known as the Diaoyu Islands in China, in the East China Sea. The 2+2 ministerial dialogue on Thursday will give New Delhi and Tokyo opportunity to review progress on the transfer of Japan’s UNICORN integrated communications antenna system to India. The system combines multiple antennas into a single structure, reducing the radar signature of naval vessels while improving communications capabilities. The transfer, once completed, would mark a significant step forward in defence technology cooperation between the two countries and help enhance the stealth capabilities of Indian Navy warships. Singh on Wednesday visited the Japan Maritime Self-Defence Force’s naval base at Yokosuka along with Koizumi and toured the Mogami-class multi-mission frigate JS Natori. Singh said that the growing maritime cooperation between the two countries reflected their deep trust and shared commitment to a free, open and rules-based Indo-Pacific. Singh and Koizumi had in August this year signed a Memorandum of Arrangement providing for greater cooperation between the Indian Navy and Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force, including information-sharing on maritime domain awareness, search and rescue, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief. The arrangement also envisages greater coordination to protect sea lanes through mutual naval visits, joint exercises, personnel exchanges and logistical support, including the use of ports and maintenance and repair facilities. The two sides also agreed to pursue reciprocal provision of ship-repair facilities. India and Japan are also expected to explore cooperation in mine-countermeasure capabilities, joint naval shipbuilding and design, ship repair and maintenance, and the development of advanced defence technologies. They are likely to review progress in joint exercises, intelligence-sharing, defence equipment collaboration and research in emerging areas such as unmanned systems, artificial intelligence and autonomous platforms. The India-Japan ministerial talks on Thursday will coincide with Trump’s meeting with Xi in Shenzhen, adding to the geopolitical significance of the dialogue at a time of uncertainty over long-term commitment of Washington, D.C., to the Indo-Pacific, where China’s hegemonic and expansionist ambitions have heightened concerns among countries in the region. Trump on Tuesday joined Narendra Modi and Sanae Takaichi, the prime ministers of India and Japan, respectively, as well as Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at the seventh Quad summit in Manila. The four leaders opposed economic coercion and destabilising or unilateral actions in the Indo-Pacific region. The bloc, however, refrained from sending any strong message to Beijing or signalling a tougher strategic security posture against China, with Trump appearing more keen to manage the US-China rivalry through direct engagement with Xi, prioritising transactional trade deals and economic gains over sustained strategic competition. Jaishankar on Wednesday said that the changing geopolitical environment had made closer cooperation between India and Japan even more compelling, with both countries placing greater emphasis on economic security, self-reliance and trusted partnerships. He said that the two countries could complement each other in areas such as advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, critical minerals, clean energy, pharmaceuticals and artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Minister M B Patil announces plans to establish model startup parks on 1,000 acres near Bengaluru
articles.summary: Bengaluru: Large and Medium Industries Minister M B Patil on Wednesday announced plans to establish model startup parks spread across 1,000 acres near Bengaluru and 100–200 acres near Hubballi-Dharwad to further strengthen the startup ecosystem in Karnataka. At an interactive session with startup founders and investors at the Bengaluru Tech Summit on Wednesday, he heard their concerns and suggestions. He also visited two stalls at the summit to familiarise himself with the products and services on display. Speaking after the interaction, Patil said some startup founders had pointed out that land prices in Bengaluru had risen sharply and that access to land at affordable rates would greatly benefit them. To address this concern, the Government was considering setting up startup parks in both regions of the State. The next steps would be decided after examining the various ways in which the necessary support could be extended, he said. There are more than 200 electric two-wheeler manufacturers in the country. Of these, four companies sell more than 100 vehicles a month, and all four have their design operations in Bengaluru. Karnataka showcases 50 startup products at Bengaluru Tech Summit However, three of them manufacture their vehicles outside Karnataka, while only one has a manufacturing facility in the State. Some startup founders attributed this to the lack of affordable land. Responding to their concerns, Patil assured them that the Government would work towards establishing dedicated startup parks. The Government was aware that it would be difficult for entrepreneurs to bear the entire investment burden on their own, Patil said. It would examine the possibility of allotting industrial plots in the proposed startup parks under a lease-cum-sale arrangement or through other suitable mechanisms. The Government would also consider providing an additional five per cent subsidy to startups located beyond Bengaluru, over and above the assistance currently available, he said. Single window for 130 services The Government aims to bring more than 130 services under the single-window clearance system. Of these, 116 services are already available, while the remaining 10–15 services are expected to be brought under its ambit within a month. Steps would be taken to ensure that the single-window system functions effectively in the true sense. He also stressed the need to revise the curricula of technical education institutions in line with industry requirements. Responding to a query from a startup founder, Patil said setting up testing facilities for aircraft, drones and fighter jets involved substantial expenditure. The Government would examine the possible support it could extend in this regard. Prashanth Prakash, Chairman of the Government's Startup Vision Group, said Karnataka had a strong ecosystem for startups. He urged entrepreneurs to look beyond design and manufacturing and also take up the production of machinery and equipment required for manufacturing activities within the State. This would help reduce costs, he emphasised. Representatives of 23 companies participated in the interaction. They included Arjun Rao of Speciale Invest, Rohan Shetty, Partner at Samsung Ventures, Shashikumar of Akshayakalpa, Nagendra and Nagaraj, founders of QpiAI, and Sumanth Krishna, Director of Simplifai. Entrepreneur Madan Padaki moderated the session. S. Selvakumar, Principal Secretary, Department of Large and Medium Industries, Commissioner Khushbu Goyal and other officials were present.

articles.title: Karnataka: Murugesh Nirani challenges Rizwan Arshad to conduct transparent tests on ethanol blending in petrol
articles.summary: Mysuru: Former minister and BJP state vice-president Murugesh Nirani challenged Karnataka government and Food and Civil Supplies Minister Rizwan Arshad to conduct the tests in a transparent way to prove that more than 20% ethanol is blended in petrol. Addressing a media conference, in Mysuru, on Wednesday, Nirani said the Karnataka government and Arshad are doing politics in the ethanol blending issue to unnecessarily blame the Centre. “They are using the ethanol issue as diversion tactics, to divert the attention of the people and media from the real problems of the people,” he said. Largest producer Nirani claimed to be the largest manufacturer of ethanol in the whole of Asia, with all his industries put together producing 28 lakh litres of ethanol daily. Stating that the average price of ethanol is Rs 62 per litre, some 4% lesser than petrol (price charged to dealers, including freight and oil company margin, in Delhi on Wednesday – Rs 69.80 per litre), Nirani said neither the oil company nor the bunk owner will make profits by mixing more ethanol. “Let Arshad form committees, comprising respective district officers, representatives of oil companies and scientists from labs, to extract samples and conduct tests. If any bunk or oil marketing company is proved guilty, nobody can stop their punishment,” Nirani said. Ethanol blending history has Mysuru links, says BJP state vice-president Murugesh Nirani Drawbacks Nirani admitted that blending of ethanol with petrol reduces mileage by around 4% and increases the rate of wear and tear in older vehicles, which are not E-10 or E-20 compatible. “However, ethanol is a saviour at this hour of crisis, due to the wars in West Asia and the erstwhile USSR. In comparison with the hike in fuel price in other nations, the price of petrol would have crossed Rs 125 per litre, without ethanol, in India. Ethanol is saving our precious foreign exchange,” he said. In reply to a question if the ethanol blending policy is formulated to help Union Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari, Nirani said, “In fact, I am the largest producer of ethanol in the entire Asia, while Gadkari’s companies, in partnership with his friends, would produce not more than 2 lakh litres. The total production of ethanol, in over 500 industries across India, is 2,040 crore litres. There is profit for all these companies and the farmers supplying sugarcane, maize and paddy to these companies. It is not just for Gadkari or any single individual,” he said. Ex-MLA C S Niranjan Kumar, state BJP minority morcha president Dr Anil Thomas, ex-mayor Sathish Swamy, Cable Mahesh, and Mahesh Raje Urs were present.

According to Pew, Muslim women had an average fertility rate of 3.1 children during 2020–2025, compared with 2.5 among Christian women. Women belonging to other religious groups had an average of 1.6 children, significantly below the replacement-level fertility rate of 2.1 children per woman needed to maintain a stable population across generations. The world’s total population is projected to increase by 29 per cent between 2020 and 2070. Muslims and Christians are the only religious groups analysed that are expected to keep pace, with Christians growing by 30 per cent and Muslims by 80 per cent. On the other hand, Hindu and Jews are projected to decline as a percentage of the global population.
